estate_label: AI, data, and compute infrastructure estate
domain: algorithmic systems, cloud services, models, chips, data centers, data brokers, government deployments, and compute procurement
scope: Government and regulated uses of algorithmic tools, AI and data suppliers, cloud-authorized services, foundation and application models, data brokers, chips, compute clusters, data centers, deployment contracts, assurance records, and public transparency inventories. The estate distinguishes vendor, product, authorization, deployment, data source, model, compute, and decision use.
why_new_estate: UK state-market, defense, regulatory, research, and industrial-policy estates all encounter AI vendors and compute infrastructure, but no current estate owns the system-level deployment chain.

denominator_contract.unit: one named algorithmic or compute system, service, deployment, or authorized offering keyed by stable product and agency identifiers
denominator_contract.inclusion_rule: Official algorithmic records, cloud authorizations, contracts, agency inventories, public impact documents, data-center and utility dockets, and corporate filings.
denominator_contract.exclusion_rule: Generic AI claims, capability announcements without deployment, model similarity, or shared cloud provider as evidence of shared data.
denominator_contract.time_window: historical through 2026-07-23, with each source query recording its own bounded window
required_null_controls: authorized service with no located agency deployment
recorded pilot not moved to production
agency with no record under bounded mandatory inventory

source_routes.bounded_output: FedRAMP authorized, ready, and in-process cloud service offerings, agencies, authorizations, impact levels, and package identifiers.
source_routes.residual_fog: Authorization is not procurement or deployment; agency use, system boundary, data, subcontractors, and current status require separate records.

source_routes.bounded_output: Published algorithmic-transparency records for in-scope central-government tools, including owner, supplier, purpose, phase, data, and risk/impact descriptions.
source_routes.residual_fog: Mandatory scope and exemptions do not create a complete all-government denominator; nonpublication is not proof of no tool.

source_routes.bounded_output: Agency AI use-case inventories, governance documents, risk classifications, retired uses, and responsible offices where published.
source_routes.residual_fog: Inventory formats and historical coverage vary; vendor, model, data, authorization, and contract joins remain.

source_routes.bounded_output: Award and transaction identifiers with separate ceiling, obligation, and outlay fields.
source_routes.residual_fog: Recipient identity, award hierarchy, subaward coverage, and performance reconciliation remain estate-specific.

source_routes.bounded_output: Contract opportunities, award notices, solicitation identifiers, and contracting data.
source_routes.residual_fog: Some APIs require a key; attachments, amendments, interested vendors, and source-selection files may require additional acquisition.

source_routes.bounded_output: CIKs, accession numbers, filing types, Form D offerings, ownership, merger, and company filings.
source_routes.residual_fog: CIK resolution, filer/entity boundaries, amended filings, and governance-right extraction require estate-specific parsing.

source_routes.bounded_output: FERC dockets, accession numbers, filings, issuances, orders, maps, forms, parties, document dates, filed dates, and posted dates.
source_routes.residual_fog: Docket metadata does not establish construction or operation; CEII, privileged, protected, legacy, and state-jurisdiction records may be unavailable.

decisive_output: system-level ledger of owner, vendor, model, data, compute, authorization, contract, deployment phase, users, impacts, and retirement or nondeployment controls
next_acquisition: freeze public AI-system and cloud-service denominators and join system, vendor, model, data, compute, contract, deployment, and assurance records
boundaries: A cloud authorization, model capability, vendor contract, algorithmic record, and deployed decision system are separate states. Shared infrastructure does not establish data sharing or common purpose.
A surveyed and prepared estate is not an acquired, completed, or finding-bearing estate.
Official source availability is not evidence of a subject overlap.
